description:
Compatibility-friendly bridge that exposes the kernel FlowEngine to Spring beans
        as a structured asynchronous / saga programming model — without making
        Spring @Async (or any thread-pool task executor) the canonical execution path
        for compensable, parkable, or event-triggered work.

        Key capabilities (default-off):
          - FlowEngineSupplier: deferred ScopedValue accessor pattern.
          - ExerisFlowProperties: enabled + persistenceEnabled + choreographyEnabled
            + requireEngine configuration flags.
          - ExerisFlowAutoConfiguration: wires template, registrar, and engine supplier
            from ExerisRuntimeLifecycle.getFlowEngine().
          - ExerisFlowDefinition: interface for Spring beans declaring kernel FlowDefinitions
            through FlowDefinitionBuilder + FlowStepAction lambdas.
          - ExerisFlowTemplate: imperative invocation surface for Spring beans — schedule,
            park, wake, lookupParked, stats, and plan registry.
          - ExerisFlowDefinitionRegistrar: lifecycle bean compiling plans and populating
            the template plan registry.
          - ExerisFlowChoreographyBridge: opt-in event-driven flow trigger discovering
            ExerisFlowChoreographyMapper beans and registering them with the kernel.

        Activation:
          exeris.runtime.flow.enabled = true (matchIfMissing = false)
          exeris.runtime.flow.choreography-enabled = true (opt-in)

        Hard rules:
          - @Async is NOT a workaround for missing flow capability.
          - Durable snapshot persistence (FlowSnapshotStore) is not enabled by default;
            persistenceEnabled defaults to false.
          - Step lambdas closing over Spring beans must not invert lifecycle
            ownership — flow lifecycle stays kernel-owned.
          - Choreography mapper beans receive only an EventDescriptor (routing
            metadata) — no payload, no scheduler reference. Implementations stay
            implementation-blind to the broker.
          - No HTTP / web / persistence concerns in this module.
